title: The Database Keeps Dying
symptom: The app team says postgres 'just dies' — no errors in its own logs, it's simply gone. It died again 20 minutes ago. Restarting it has been tried; it doesn't stay up.

options: A bug in this PostgreSQL version
A batch job consumed most of the RAM, so the kernel's OOM killer chose postgres
Someone ran 'systemctl stop postgres' by mistake

debrief: A process that vanishes with nothing in its own logs was usually killed from outside — and dmesg recorded the OOM killer doing it. 'ps aux --sort=-%mem' showed the real culprit: a java batch job with an 8GB heap on a machine that can't afford it. Restarting postgres alone just fed it back to the OOM killer. Fixes: size the batch job's heap to the machine, move batch work off the database host, and protect postgres with OOMScoreAdjust (linux-incident-003 walks through the same pattern).
